stimulus.source_note: Thomas Mun, England's Treasure by Forraign Trade (1664), ch. 2. Quotation verbatim; figures from Mun's own example in the same chapter.
stimulus.text:
The ordinary means therefore to increase our wealth and treasure is by Forraign Trade, wherein wee must ever observe this rule; to sell more to strangers yearly than wee consume of theirs in value.

| England's yearly trade | Pounds |
| Exports | £2,200,000 |
| Imports | £2,000,000 |
| Net gain in treasure | £200,000 |

primary_sources: Thomas Mun, England's Treasure by Forraign Trade (1664)

stem: Thomas Mun, an English merchant, wrote the passage below in 1664. According to Mun, what must a kingdom do to increase its wealth and treasure?

options.text: Conquer colonies and seize their gold by force of arms
options.misconception: Confuses mercantilist trade policy with conquest; Mun's argument is about selling, not seizing.

options.text: Sell more to foreigners each year than it buys from them
Refuse to trade with any foreign nation at all
options.misconception: Reads 'favorable balance' as no trade at all; Mun wants more exports, not closed borders.

options.text: Enrich itself through gifts and payments from other nations
options.misconception: Substitutes tribute or gifts for trade; Mun's rule is about the balance of exports and imports.

rationales.general:
1. Start with the writer. Mun is an English merchant writing a handbook for traders in 1664.
2. Find his rule. The passage names one 'ordinary means' of increasing wealth: foreign trade.
3. Read the rule closely. Sell more to strangers each year than the kingdom consumes of theirs in value — exports must beat imports.
4. Match that rule to an option. Only selling more than you buy fits the rule he states.
Remember: when a source states a rule, test each option against the rule's exact words.
rationales.A: Mun's rule is about trade, not war. Conquest is not how his rule increases treasure — selling is.
rationales.B: Mun's rule is exact: sell more to strangers yearly than the kingdom consumes of theirs in value. Exports must beat imports.
rationales.C: Refusing to trade would stop the very trade Mun says increases wealth. His rule needs trade, not isolation.
rationales.D: Gifts and payments are not Mun's rule. He names foreign trade — selling more than buying — as the ordinary means.
